title: Morley Callaghan: Stories
text: Edward Morley Callaghan was a Canadian novelist, short story writer, playwright, and TV and radio personality.

title: Timothy Findley: The Last of the Crazy People
text: Timothy Irving Frederick Findley was a Canadian novelist and playwright. He was also informally known by the nickname Tiff or Tiffy, an acronym of his initials.

title: Hugh Hood: The Camera Always Lies
text: Hugh John Blagdon Hood, OC was a Canadian novelist, short story writer, essayist and university professor. Hood wrote 32 books: 17 novels including the 12-volume New Age novel sequence (influenced by Marcel Proust and Anthony Powell), several volumes of short fiction, and 5 of nonfiction.

title: Farley Mowat: The Polar Passion
text: Farley McGill Mowat was a Canadian writer and environmentalist. His works were translated into 52 languages, and he sold more than 17 million books.

title: Margaret Atwood, The Circle Game, won a Governor General's award and "sold out immediately"
text: Margaret Eleanor Atwood is a Canadian novelist, poet, literary critic, and inventor. Since 1961, she has published 18 books of poetry, 18 novels, 11 books of nonfiction, nine collections of short fiction, eight children's books, two graphic novels, and a number of small press editions of both poetry and fiction.

title: John Robert Colombo, Abracadabra
text: John Robert Colombo is a Canadian writer, editor, and poet. He has published over 200 titles, including major anthologies and reference works.

title: D. G. Jones, Phrases from Orpheus
text: Douglas Gordon "D. G." Jones was a Canadian poet, translator and educator. Born in Bancroft, Ontario, Jones was educated at the private school of Lakefield College School in Ontario, at McGill University and at Queen's University.

title: Dorothy Livesay, The Unquiet Bed, Canadian and African experiences
text: Dorothy Kathleen May Livesay, was a Canadian poet who twice won the Governor General's Award in the 1940s, and was "senior woman writer in Canada" during the 1970s and 1980s.

title: Michael Ondaatje, The Dainty Monsters, Toronto: Coach House Press
text: Philip Michael Ondaatje is a Sri Lankan-born Canadian poet, fiction writer and essayist. Ondaatje's literary career began with his poetry: in 1967 he published The Dainty Monsters, and in 1970 the critically acclaimed The Collected Works of Billy the Kid.

title: P. K. Page, Cry Ararat!: Poems New and Selected
text: Patricia Kathleen Page, was a Canadian poet, though the citation as she was inducted as a Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada reads "poet, novelist, script writer, playwright, essayist, journalist, librettist, teacher and artist." She was the author of more than 30 published books that include poetry, fiction, travel diaries, essays, children's books, and an autobiography. As a visual artist, she exhibited her w…

title: Al Purdy, North of Summer, a diary in verse recounting his stay on Baffin Island
text: Alfred Wellington Purdy was a 20th-century Canadian free verse poet. Purdy's writing career spanned fifty-six years.

title: Raymond Souster, editor, New Wave Canada anthology of younger poets
text: Raymond Holmes Souster was a Canadian poet whose writing career spanned over 70 years. More than 50 volumes of his own poetry were published during his lifetime, and he edited or co-edited a dozen volumes of poetry by others.

title: Miriam Waddington, The Glass Trumpet
text: Miriam Waddington was a Canadian poet, short story writer and translator. She was part of a Montreal literary circle that included F. R. Scott, Irving Layton and Louis Dudek.

title: George Woodcock, Selected Poems of George Woodcock, Toronto: Clarke, Irwin, Canada
text: George Woodcock was a Canadian writer of political biography and history, an anarchist thinker, a philosopher, an essayist and literary critic. He was also a poet and published several volumes of travel writing.

title: See 1967 Governor General's Awards for a complete list of winners and finalists for those awards.
text: Each winner of the 1967 Governor General's Awards for Literary Merit was selected by a panel of judges administered by the Canada Council for the Arts. The winners were awarded a cash prize of $2500.

title: Stephen Leacock Award: Richard J. Needham, Needham's Inferno
text: The Stephen Leacock Memorial Medal for Humour, also known as the Stephen Leacock Medal for Humour or just the Leacock Medal, is an annual Canadian literary award presented for the best book of humour written in English by a Canadian writer, published or self-published in the previous year. The silver medal, designed by sculptor Emanuel Hahn, is a tribute to well-known Canadian humorist Stephen Leacock and is accom…
wiki: Stephen Leacock Memorial Medal for Humour

title: Vicky Metcalf Award: John Patrick Gillese
text: The Vicky Metcalf Award for Literature for Young People, colloquially called the Vicky, is given annually at the Writers' Trust Awards to a writer or illustrator whose body of work has been "inspirational to Canadian youth". It is a top honour for Canadian children's writers and Canadian children's book illustrators.
wiki: Vicky Metcalf Award for Literature for Young People

title: Norman Jewison's In the Heat of the Night premieres
text: Norman Frederick Jewison was a Canadian filmmaker. He is known for directing films which addressed topical social and political issues, often making controversial or complicated subjects accessible to mainstream audiences.

title: Michael Snow's Wavelength premieres and starts the structural film movement.
text: Michael James Aleck Snow was a Canadian artist who worked in a range of media including film, installation, sculpture, photography, and music. His best-known films are Wavelength (1967) and La Région Centrale (1971), with the former regarded as a milestone in avant-garde cinema.

title: Mr. Dressup
text: Mr. Dressup is a Canadian children's television series, starring Ernie Coombs, a former understudy of Fred Rogers, in the title role.

title: O'Keefe Centre Presents
text: O'Keefe Centre Presents is a series of Canadian variety specials which aired on CBC Television from 1967 to 1968.

title: Man Alive
text: Man Alive is a Canadian television program exploring faith and spirituality. The program premiered in 1967 on CBC Television.

title: The Pig and Whistle
text: The Pig and Whistle is a Canadian musical television series aired on the CTV television network from 1967 to 1977. Filmed in Toronto, Ontario but set in a fictional English pub, the show featured an assortment of Canadian, British and Irish performers.
